variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Memcached is a networked, in-memory key-value cache. An application gives it an opaque key, a value, and usually an expiration time; a later request for that key can avoid a slower database query, API call, or rendering step.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Opaque key and value
pairs.detail: The server does not understand rows, JSON fields, relationships, or business versions.
pairs.explanation: The server does not understand rows, JSON fields, relationships, or business versions. The client serializes a bounded value and chooses a stable key.

pairs.label: Memory is a budget
pairs.explanation: Values occupy slab-class chunks. Expiration and eviction keep use bounded, while item shape and access frequency determine what remains resident.

pairs.label: Clients own placement
pairs.detail: A client library commonly hashes each key to one server.
pairs.explanation: A client library commonly hashes each key to one server. Consistent hashing limits how many keys move when the pool changes.

pairs.label: Misses are normal
pairs.detail: Every read path needs a bounded source fallback.
pairs.explanation: Every read path needs a bounded source fallback. Hit rate changes latency and source load, but it must never decide whether the answer is correct.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Memcached is a networked, in-memory key-value cache. An application gives it an opaque key, a value, and usually an expiration time; a later request for that key can avoid a slower database query, API call, or rendering step.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Expiration
pairs.detail: A TTL says when the cached copy becomes invalid.
pairs.explanation: A TTL says when the cached copy becomes invalid. In the basic text protocol, values up to 30 days are relative seconds; larger values are interpreted as Unix timestamps. Expiration is not a durable deletion guarantee.

pairs.label: Reclaim
pairs.detail: Expired items can be reclaimed by background maintenance, lookup, or allocation.
pairs.explanation: Expired items can be reclaimed by background maintenance, lookup, or allocation. The server does not need to synchronously clear every expired byte at the TTL boundary.

pairs.label: Eviction
pairs.detail: When a class needs a chunk and cannot reclaim expired space or another page, it can remove a non-expired item.
pairs.explanation: When a class needs a chunk and cannot reclaim expired space or another page, it can remove a non-expired item. An eviction is a capacity signal, not source-data loss.

Reclaim: Expired items can be reclaimed by background maintenance, lookup, or allocation.

pairs.label: Namespace the owner
pairs.detail: Begin with the service and entity, such as catalog:product, so unrelated teams cannot accidentally reuse the same key space.
pairs.explanation: Begin with the service and entity, such as catalog:product, so unrelated teams cannot accidentally reuse the same key space.

pairs.label: Include representation version
pairs.detail: Add a version such as v3 when serialization or derived fields change.
pairs.explanation: Add a version such as v3 when serialization or derived fields change. Old keys can expire naturally instead of requiring a dangerous global flush.

pairs.label: Choose freshness
pairs.detail: Derive TTL from acceptable staleness and source recovery cost.
pairs.explanation: Derive TTL from acceptable staleness and source recovery cost. Invalidate or move the version after authoritative writes when waiting for TTL would violate the contract.

pairs.label: Bound refill ownership
pairs.detail: Choose single-flight, a short lease, early recache, or stale serving so a popular key does not multiply source work at expiration.

pairs.label: Read and write values
pairs.detail: get returns one or more present values.
pairs.explanation: get returns one or more present values. set writes regardless of prior existence; add writes only when absent. delete invalidates a key but cannot coordinate an external database transaction.

pairs.label: Guard concurrent updates
pairs.explanation: gets returns a CAS token. cas stores only if that token still matches, allowing a client to detect an intervening cache update instead of blindly overwriting it.

pairs.label: Coordinate modern refill
pairs.detail: Meta commands can expose TTL and item metadata, elect a recache winner, support early recache, and intentionally serve stale data while revalidation runs.

pairs.label: Choose Memcached
pairs.detail: Use it for simple, high-volume cache-aside reads where values are opaque, misses are safe, and client-side placement plus application-owned coherence are acceptable.
pairs.explanation: Use it for simple, high-volume cache-aside reads where values are opaque, misses are safe, and client-side placement plus application-owned coherence are acceptable.

pairs.label: Choose Redis or another data service
pairs.detail: Use a different system when the design depends on durable state, replication semantics, server-side data structures, streams, transactions, or richer atomic workflows.
pairs.explanation: Use a different system when the design depends on durable state, replication semantics, server-side data structures, streams, transactions, or richer atomic workflows.

pairs.label: Choose a CDN or HTTP cache
pairs.detail: Use an HTTP-aware cache when validators, request headers, status codes, shared-cache directives, geographic delivery, and purge behavior are the core contract.
pairs.explanation: Use an HTTP-aware cache when validators, request headers, status codes, shared-cache directives, geographic delivery, and purge behavior are the core contract.
